sampling_model.design: Exactly one regime is active. In \(\mathsf B(p)\), labels are iid categorical and units are conditionally independent Bernoulli. In \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), the label vector has fixed counts \(C_{C,k}\) and each cluster is conditionally uniform on its exact-count slice.
sampling_model.units: Observe \(C\) independent equal-size cluster schedules from an unrestricted bounded \([0,1]\)-valued potential-outcome law, with no interference across clusters and arbitrary interference within a cluster.
sampling_model.treatment: The schedule law \(P\) is mapped to observed data by the known kernel \(R_{B,p}\) or the joint fixed-count kernel \(R^{CR}_{C_C}\); scores and influence functions live in the induced observed-law spaces.
sampling_model.overlap: Interior rational saturations make every Bernoulli hit rate positive. Active-face CR results require positive shares only on \(A\); the full-vector CR CLT and all-policy rank theorem require \(\alpha_k>0\) for every reported policy.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate assignment-specific means and variances within realized target cells, average cells uniformly within each exact-count slice, and use a prespecified bounded fallback for empty cells. Covariance-driven selection may use sample splitting.

tldr: The headline result prices the loss from using Bernoulli-label data to select the welfare-maximizing exact-count policy: on every declared tied-best face, the optimized best-policy simple-regret ratio is bounded by active exact-hit mass with an exact equality frontier, and the squared ratio gives the cluster-count penalty. Separate observed-law theorems establish finite-sample nuisance deletion, full-menu calibrated CLTs, active-face LAN lower experiments, and tie-valid rank inference. The closest same-target estimator is transcribed exactly from Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1); its derived influence variance reveals cross-label, assignment-cell, and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses. For a non-symmetric three-policy menu, exact arithmetic reports the hit matrix, its column masses, and its unique maximum-mass normalized column; the general certified routine supplies optimizer and risk enclosures once a variance vector and tolerance are specified, but no executed numerical transcript is reported here. A screened hierarchical construction certifies the noncompact general-K game across retained partial-tie faces and uniformly positive-definite covariance cells, with explicit zero-rate boundary handling and full quotient-ball primitive transfer.

project_justification.gap: Same-target saturation-ranking work uses the nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson estimator in Appendix-B Eq. (S1) and a rule-specific regret envelope; it does not give all-rule nuisance deletion, observed-law target tangents, a sharp face-specific mechanism-deficiency frontier, or a validated noncompact Gaussian outer-design implementation.
project_justification.niche: Exact-count deployment exposes the known hit polytope \(B\Delta_K\) inside an unrestricted within-cluster interference model. Treating common welfare as a nuisance and passing both means and observations to their contrast quotient allows the assignment mechanism itself to be priced for the same causal target.
project_justification.fill: The project makes mechanism loss the sole headline, derives its observed-score and efficiency foundations, proves the exact Han variance comparison, and couples a Joo-informed Gaussian selector to calibrated cluster data. Its certified screened hierarchy handles unbounded contrasts by enumerating retained subfaces, transfers each full compact quotient ball through a surjective representative set, and certifies both outer allocation problems on their stated positive-rate domains.

interpretation: The causal object is the finite-population-style exact-slice welfare vector, while \(B\), \(q=Bp\), the calibrated estimator, and the Gaussian game are respectively design, observed-law, estimation, and decision functionals.  Their relationship is proved: exact hits supply information \(q_k/\tau_k^2\), calibration removes the between-assignment mean component, local asymptotic normality transfers the experiment to the translation-quotient Gaussian game, and the certified optimizer converts the resulting risk into a prospective allocation.  Thus the mechanism penalty is a loss of assignment information for the same causal target, not a change of estimand.
technical_internal_limitation: The noncompact routine is uniform over the finitely many retained subsets inside a declared face and over compact positive-definite covariance cells. Bernoulli hit positivity supplies the full outer-simplex transfer. Exact-count primitive transfer is restricted to compact positive-share allocation sets; at an action-relevant zero share only the proved extended value \(+\infty\) is asserted.
honest_scope: The results concern fixed \(n\), fixed \(K\), equal cluster sizes, distinct interior rational saturations, isolated iid cluster schedules, and exact-slice welfare. Bernoulli-label and exact-count complete randomization are mutually exclusive regimes, and all scores are defined under their induced observed laws. Active-face CR results allow zero inactive shares, but the full-menu CR CLT and rank theorem require every reported share to be positive. At a unique best policy first-order local regret is zero. When \(K=2\), the face game reduces to the classical sign rule and Neyman allocation; assignment-homogeneous slice means eliminate the calibration component but not necessarily the Horvitz--Thompson participation term in Eq. (S1). The finite positive-face Gaussian certificate is a theorem target; the three-policy calculation reports only exact hit-matrix and column-mass arithmetic, not an executed optimizer or risk certificate. The Kenya design is a prospective design consumer rather than an authorized reanalysis. For the Appendix-B Eq. (S1) comparator, the note matches the published equal-size, finite-interior-menu, iid-cluster, bounded-outcome, unrestricted within-cluster-interference class, while dropping unnecessary smoothness and allowing boundary nominal-label shares via cross-label hits. Han–Owusu–Shin’s broader main complete-randomization envelope also permits heterogeneous integral cluster sizes; the present equal-size converse transfers upward as a lower bound on that broader class, but the efficient upper construction, single hit map, and exact mechanism frontier are not claimed there.

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: The number of mutually isolated sampled clusters.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The fixed number of units in every cluster.

symbols.name: K
symbols.def: The fixed number of exact-count policies.

symbols.name: \mathcal A
symbols.def: \(\mathcal A=\mathcal K\), so one exact-count policy is selected.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: A schedule containing one bounded potential outcome for every unit and every within-cluster assignment.

symbols.name: Y_j(z)
symbols.def: The bounded outcome of unit \(j\) under within-cluster assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: An otherwise unrestricted law of the bounded cluster schedule \(Y\).

symbols.name: Y_c
symbols.def: The bounded schedule drawn for cluster \(c\in\{1,\ldots,C\}\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_K)\) is chosen before sampling and may lie on the boundary of \(\Delta_K\).

symbols.name: L_c
symbols.def: The first-stage label of cluster \(c\), generated according to exactly one of the regimes \(\mathsf B(p)\) and \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\).

symbols.name: Z_c
symbols.def: The realized within-cluster assignment of cluster \(c\), generated conditionally on \(L_c\) by the active randomization regime.

symbols.name: O_c^{\mathrm{hit}}
symbols.def: The record retaining \(L_c,Z_c\), retaining the observed bounded outcome vector when \(Z_c\in\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\mathcal S_k\), and replacing it by \(\star\) otherwise.

symbols.name: \mathcal L
symbols.def: A bounded loss \(\mathcal L(U,a)\) depending on the schedule law only through \(U=(U_1,\ldots,U_K)\).

symbols.name: \widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}
symbols.def: \(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}=\bigl(\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\bigr)^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c)\), with fallback \(1/2\) when the denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \mathsf B(p)
symbols.def: Independently draw \(L_c\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p)\), then conditionally assign the coordinates of \(Z_c\) independently as \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_{L_c})\).

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: \(\alpha_k=\lim_{C\to\infty}C_{C,k}/C\), whenever the displayed limit is invoked.

symbols.name: \mathsf{CR}(\alpha)
symbols.def: Draw \(L=(L_1,\ldots,L_C)\) uniformly over label vectors with exactly \(C_{C,k}\) copies of label \(k\), then conditionally draw \(Z_c\) uniformly on \(\mathcal S_{L_c}\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak D_C
symbols.def: All measurable randomized rules mapping the indicated experiment to one action in \(\mathcal A\).

symbols.name: P_0
symbols.def: A bounded-schedule law whose assignment-specific outcome-vector marginals have positive average variance on each active target slice.

symbols.name: P_{0,z}
symbols.def: The \(P_0\)-marginal law of the observed bounded outcome vector under assignment \(z\).

symbols.name: \underline\tau
symbols.def: A fixed lower bound for active calibrated slice standard deviations.

symbols.name: v_A
symbols.def: \(v_A=(v_k)_{k\in A}\), with \(v_k=\tau_k^2(P_0)\) in the exact-hit application.

symbols.name: r_A
symbols.def: \(r_A=(r_k)_{k\in A}\); positive coordinates define the Gaussian experiment, and action-relevant boundary zeros are interpreted through the lower-semicontinuous value.

symbols.name: s_{A,\max}
symbols.type: largest active hit mass of one nominal label

symbols.name: t
symbols.type: first nominal-label share for two policies

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}
symbols.def: The empirical second moment of all \(K\) calibrated influence coordinates, using estimated hit rates under \(\mathsf B(p)\) and the fixed shares \(C_{C,k}/C\) under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), with the prespecified bounded fallback on undefined cells.

symbols.name: \mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)
symbols.type: simultaneous confidence set for policy rank
symbols.def: Invert all studentized pairwise intervals from the calibrated estimates and \(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\); return \(\{1,\ldots,K\}\) if a required target assignment cell is empty.

symbols.name: \varepsilon
symbols.def: The requested deterministic gap between the Gaussian upper and lower certificates.

symbols.name: R_{B,p}
symbols.space: \(\text{Markov kernels from schedules to observed records}\)
symbols.def: The known kernel that draws \(L\sim\operatorname{Categorical}(p)\), draws the coordinates of \(Z\) independently as \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_L)\), and returns \(O=(L,Z,Y(Z))\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)
symbols.def: The image of \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\) under coordinatewise reduction \(O_c\mapsto O_c^{\mathrm{hit}}\).

symbols.name: R^{CR}_{C_C}
symbols.space: \(\text{Markov kernels from schedule arrays to observed arrays}\)
symbols.def: The known kernel that draws a label vector uniformly with counts \(C_C=(C_{C,k})_k\), conditionally draws \(Z_c\) uniformly on \(\mathcal S_{L_c}\), and returns \((O_c)_{c=1}^C\).

symbols.name: Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}
symbols.def: \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}=P^{\otimes C}R^{CR}_{C_C}\); conditionally on the randomized fixed-count label vector, it is the product of its stratum-specific observed laws.

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)=Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\), indexed by the fixed count vector \(C_C=(C_{C,k})_{k\in\mathcal K}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)
symbols.def: The image of \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\) that retains each realized exact-count assignment and outcome vector while deleting the randomized label vector.

symbols.name: \widehat\Sigma_{C,A}
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}=(\widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)})_{AA}\) whenever the full estimator is defined, or the same empirical score construction restricted directly to active coordinates.

symbols.name: H_A
symbols.def: \(H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\); a zero-sum vector is only one representative and is not itself observed.

symbols.name: h
symbols.def: \(h=(h_k)_{k\in A}\) is a full local displacement; its decision-relevant class is \([h]\in H_A\), while its common-shift coordinate remains a nuisance in the statistical experiment.

symbols.name: P_{t,h,z}
symbols.def: For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(k\in A\), it satisfies \(dP_{t,h,z}/dP_{0,z}(y)=\exp\{t h_k(W(y)-\mu_z)/\tau_k^2-\Lambda_{z,k}(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\}\); nontarget marginals equal \(P_{0,z}\).

symbols.name: \bar P_{t,h}
symbols.def: \(\bar P_{t,h}=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{t,h,z}\); at \(t=0\), \(\bar P_0\) and \(P_0\) induce the same observed law under either regime.

symbols.name: D_A
symbols.def: With \(a_0=\min A\), the rows of \(D_A\) are \(e_k^{\prime}-e_{a_0}^{\prime}\) for \(k\in A\setminus\{a_0\}\); thus \(D_A\mathbf 1_A=0\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(D_A)=|A|-1\).

symbols.name: \lVert[h]\rVert_A
symbols.def: \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A=\lVert D_Ah\rVert_2\), which is independent of the representative of \([h]\in H_A\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A fixed finite bound in \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\); it does not bound the common-location nuisance.

symbols.name: G_A(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: For positive rates, the infimum over all measurable randomized selectors of the supremum over full \(h\in\mathbb R^A\) in \(X\sim N\{h,\Sigma(v_A,r_A)\}\) under loss \(\max_kh_k-h_a\); at boundary rates it is the lower-semicontinuous closure.

symbols.name: R_{CR,A}^\star
symbols.def: \(R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)=\min_{a\in\Delta_A}G_A(v_A,a)\); boundary coercivity places every minimizer in \(\Delta_A^\circ\).

symbols.name: \delta_{\varepsilon,A}
symbols.def: A finite-partition selector certified on quotient radius \(M\) and a rational uniformly positive-definite covariance cell, with all action-cell and tail errors included in its receipt.

symbols.name: G_{A,M}(v_A,r_A)
symbols.type: compact quotient Gaussian minimax simple-regret value
symbols.def: The invariant-selector value obtained from \(G_A(v_A,r_A)\) by restricting \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\), equivalently the quotient experiment \(D_AX\sim N(D_Ah,\Omega_A)\) on that ball.

symbols.name: L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: The finite-prior Bayes value minus outward quadrature, truncation, grid, covariance, and rounding errors for the fixed radius \(M\).

symbols.name: U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)
symbols.def: The global-on-the-quotient-ball risk bound for \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\), including parameter, covariance, action-cell, quadrature, Gaussian-tail, and rounding errors.

symbols.name: \mathfrak C_K
symbols.def: The certified hierarchical noncompact routine on a declared candidate face A: it uses an independent Gaussian screen–decision split, applies certified compact quotient selectors to every retained nonempty subset, and certifies the outer design over the Bernoulli hit polytope or exact-count simplex by rational branch-and-bound. definitions.name: mutually exclusive assignment regimes
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf B(p)\) draws iid categorical labels and conditionally independent unit assignments, whereas \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) draws one fixed-count label vector and conditionally uniform exact-slice assignments; every result invokes exactly one regime.

definitions.name: schedule-to-observation laws
definitions.construction: In regime \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(Q^B_{P,p}=P R_{B,p}\) and the sample law is \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\). In regime \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}=P^{\otimes C}R^{CR}_{C_C}\), equivalently the conditional product of stratum-specific observed laws given the randomized fixed-count label vector.

definitions.name: full and reduced regime experiments
definitions.construction: \((\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p),\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p))\) are \((Q^B_{P,p})^{\otimes C}\) and its target-hit image; \((\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha),\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha))\) are \(Q^{CR}_{P,C_C}\) and its label-deleted image.

definitions.name: assignment-calibrated exact-hit estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widetilde U_C=(\widetilde U_{C,k})_{k\in\mathcal K}\), where \(\widetilde U_{C,k}=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\overline W_z\); \(\widetilde U_{C,A}\) is its active-face restriction, with the prespecified empty-cell values inherited from \(\overline W_z\).

definitions.name: raw cross-label pooled-hit estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}\) is the ratio of the sum of observed cluster welfares on \(\mathcal S_k\) to the number of hits on \(\mathcal S_k\), with fallback \(1/2\) on a zero denominator.

definitions.name: published nominal-label estimator and efficient nominal subexperiment
definitions.construction: Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is the Horvitz--Thompson estimator \(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=(Cp_k)^{-1}\sum_c\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}[\gamma_k(Z_c)/\beta_k(Z_c)]W_c(Z_c)\). The best regular nominal-label procedure calibrates assignment cells using only \(\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\) and has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\).

definitions.name: explicit full target tangent and least-favourable submodel
definitions.construction: Set \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{0,z}\).  For every representative \(h=(h_k)_{k\in A}\in\mathbb R^A\), including every common-shift direction \(h+c\mathbf 1_A\), keep all nontarget marginals fixed and, for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\) with \(k\in A\), set \(dP_{t,h,z}/dP_{0,z}(y)=\exp\{t h_k(W(y)-\mu_z)/\tau_k^2-\Lambda_{z,k}(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\}\).  Define \(\bar P_{t,h}=\bigotimes_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}P_{t,h,z}\) and \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\).  The decision-relevant coordinate of \(h\) is its class \([h]\in H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\), but the statistical path retains the common-shift nuisance rather than fixing a representative.

definitions.name: full-location and quotient Gaussian simple-regret games
definitions.construction:
Fix \(a_0=\min A\), let \(D_A\) have rows \(e_k^{\prime}-e_{a_0}^{\prime}\), \(k\in A\setminus\{a_0\}\), and put \(H_A=\mathbb R^A/\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1_A\}\) and \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A=\lVert D_Ah\rVert_2\).  For positive \(v_A,r_A\), let \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)=\operatorname{diag}(v_k/r_k:k\in A)\) and \(\Omega_A=D_A\Sigma(v_A,r_A)D_A^{\prime}\), and define
\[
G_A(v_A,r_A)=\inf_{\delta}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A}\mathbb E_h\!\left[\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_{\delta(X)}\right],\qquad X\mid h\sim N\{h,\Sigma(v_A,r_A)\},
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable randomized selectors.  Equivalently the infimum is over location-invariant selectors \(\delta(x+c\mathbf 1_A)=\delta(x)\), hence over selectors based on \(D_AX\sim N(D_Ah,\Omega_A)\).  For \(M<\infty\), \(G_{A,M}(v_A,r_A)\) is the same invariant-selector game with \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\).  On \([0,\infty)^A\), define \(G_A\) at a boundary rate as the lower-semicontinuous closure \(\liminf_{r'\to r,\ r'>0}G_A(v_A,r')\).

definitions.name: attained face-specific optimized local design values
definitions.construction:
Using the lower-semicontinuous boundary value of \(G_A\), define
\[
R_{B,A}^\star(v_A)=\min_{p\in\Delta_K}G_A(v_A,(Bp)_A),\qquad
R_{CR,A}^\star(v_A)=\min_{a\in\Delta_A}G_A(v_A,a).
\]
Only the active coordinates are supplied to \(G_A\).  Positivity of every entry of \(B\) keeps \((Bp)_A\) in the positive orthant, whereas boundary coercivity makes every minimizer in the exact-count simplex belong to \(\Delta_A^\circ\); allocating mass to inactive exact-count policies is therefore excluded after the active face is selected.

definitions.name: exact two-policy quotient-game allocation map
definitions.construction:
For \(K=2\), write \(p=(t,1-t)\), \(q_1(t)=B_{12}+(B_{11}-B_{12})t\), and \(q_2(t)=B_{22}-(B_{22}-B_{21})t\).  Define
\[
F_v(t)=\frac{v_1}{q_1(t)}+\frac{v_2}{q_2(t)},\qquad
t^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{0\leq t\leq1}F_v(t).
\]
This is the exact contrast-variance allocation map for the two-action quotient game.  Its exact-count counterpart minimizes \(v_1/\alpha_1+v_2/(1-\alpha_1)\) over \(0<\alpha_1<1\).

definitions.name: tie-aware rank target and calibrated confidence set
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{Rank}_k(U)=\{1+\sum_{j\neq k}\mathbf 1\{U_j>U_k\},\ldots,K-\sum_{j\neq k}\mathbf 1\{U_j<U_k\}\}\), and \(\mathcal R_{C,k}(\gamma)\) is the max-\(t\) inversion with the full-rank empty-cell fallback.

definitions.name: validated compact quotient Gaussian certificate
definitions.construction: For fixed \(A\), \(M<\infty\), and a rational compact cell of positive \((v_A,r_A)\) on which \(\Omega_A\) is uniformly positive definite, form rational partitions of the quotient parameter ball \(\{g:\lVert g\rVert_2\leq M\}\), a truncated quotient-observation box, and the covariance cell.  Solve each finite parameter game by a rational finite prior and a represented randomized selector; evaluate posterior cost functions and selector risks by directed interval arithmetic; and add explicit parameter-grid, covariance-Kullback--Leibler, observation-tail, quadrature, and ambiguous-action-cell errors.  Refine until the outward-rounded outputs \(L_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\) and \(U_\varepsilon(v_A,r_A)\) bracket \(G_{A,M}(v_A,r_A)\) with gap at most \(\varepsilon\).  The returned receipt records all rational inputs, branch cells, precision, enclosures, the allocated error budget, the checker revision, and a checksum; \(\delta_{\varepsilon,A}\) is the represented quotient selector certified by that receipt.

definitions.name: certified hierarchical noncompact boundary routine
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak C_K\) is the certified hierarchical noncompact routine on a declared candidate face \(A\).  Choose \(0<\lambda<1\); split a Gaussian observation into independent screening and decision observations with covariances \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/\lambda\) and \(\Sigma(v_A,r_A)/(1-\lambda)\); retain arms within threshold \(T\) of the screening maximum; multiply the decision observation by \(\sqrt{1-\lambda}\); and apply the compact quotient certificate separately on every realized nonempty subset \(S\subseteq A\).  Optimize the resulting certified value over \(B\Delta_K\) or \(\Delta_A\) by rational branch-and-bound, excluding action-relevant zero-rate neighborhoods with the certified two-arm lower bound.  The routine adapts among retained subsets of the declared face.  Global candidate adaptation means taking \(A=\mathcal K\) with positive information for every candidate; at an action-relevant zero rate its value is \(+\infty\).

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), for every \(k,\ell\in\mathcal K\) and \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\Pr(L_c=\ell,Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/M_k\), \(\Pr(Z_c=z)=q_k/M_k\), and \(\Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/q_k\). Hence \(Z_c\mid\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\) is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\), and the target-hit count vector is multinomial with probabilities \((q_1,\ldots,q_K,1-\sum_kq_k)\).
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(c\), \(k\), \(\ell\), and \(z\in\mathcal S_k\).  The coordinate sum of \(z\) is \(m_k\).  By \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-schedule-independence}\), and \(\texttt{ass:bernoulli-units}\),
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell,Z_c=z)
 =p_\ell\pi_\ell^{m_k}(1-\pi_\ell)^{n-m_k}
 =\frac{p_\ell B_{k\ell}}{M_k}. \tag{1}
\]
Summing (1) over \(\ell\) and using \(q=Bp\) gives
\[
 \Pr(Z_c=z)=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{\ell=1}^Kp_\ell B_{k\ell}=\frac{q_k}{M_k}. \tag{2}
\]
Every \(B_{k\ell}\) is positive because \(1\leq m_k\leq n-1\) and \(0<\pi_\ell<1\).  Since \(p\in\Delta_K\), at least one \(p_\ell\) is positive, whence \(q_k>0\).  Division by (2) is therefore valid, and Bayes' identity yields
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=\frac{p_\ell B_{k\ell}}{q_k}. \tag{3}
\]
The right side of (2) is constant over the \(M_k\) elements of \(\mathcal S_k\).  Hence \(\Pr(Z_c\in\mathcal S_k)=q_k\) and \(Z_c\) is conditionally uniform on that slice.  Distinct \(m_k\)'s make the slices pairwise disjoint.  Finally the cluster labels, schedules, and conditional randomizations are independent across \(c\); thus the indicators of the \(K\) disjoint hit events and their complement are iid categorical with probabilities \((q_1,\ldots,q_K,1-\sum_kq_k)\).  Their totals have the asserted multinomial law.
statements.justification: This factorization identifies the Bernoulli information carrier and the cross-label hit rate.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix B retains the nominally matching label rather than the pooled carrier with rate \(Bp\).
statements.consumer: The Bernoulli estimator, lower experiment, and nominal-label allocation all use this factorization.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(C\), \(p\), and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf B(p)\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{full}}(p)))]
=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,B}^{\mathrm{hit}}(p)))].
\]
The equality persists after deleting \(L_c\) conditional on every realized target assignment.  More generally, the same equality holds when the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class are replaced by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and depends on the schedule law only through \(U\).  This includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  It holds for rules observing the entire outcome vector because the reverse inequality fixes every nontarget assignment marginal at a known distribution and replaces the unidentified schedule coupling by the product of its assignment-specific marginals.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(R_{\mathrm{full}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{hit}}\) denote the two minimax risks.  The hit record is a measurable image of the full record, so every hit-rule lifts to a full-rule and
\[
 R_{\mathrm{full}}\leq R_{\mathrm{hit}}. \tag{4}
\]
For each assignment \(z\), write \(F_z\) for the marginal law of \((Y_j(z))_{j=1}^n\) under \(P\).  Because \([0,1]^n\) is standard Borel and \(\mathcal Z_n\) is finite, every collection \((F_z:z\in\mathcal Z_n)\) is realized by the legal product schedule law \(\bigotimes_zF_z\).  Fix known laws \(F_z^0\) off \(\bigcup_k\mathcal S_k\), and let \(\mathcal P_0\) contain the product schedule laws having those nontarget marginals and arbitrary target marginals.  This restriction leaves unrestricted both the possible target vector \(U\) and the target-hit observed laws.

Given any randomized full-data rule \(\delta\), construct a hit-data rule \(\delta^0\) by conditionally drawing every omitted nontarget outcome vector from the known law \(F_{Z_c}^0\), independently across clusters, and applying \(\delta\) to the completed record.  Existence of this parameter-free simulation kernel follows from the standard-Borel condition.  For every \(P\in\mathcal P_0\), the completed record has exactly its full-experiment law, and hence
\[
 \mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta^0)=\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta). \tag{5}
\]
Since \(\mathcal P_0\subseteq\mathcal P\) and its target marginals exhaust the reduced parameter space,
\[
 \sup_P\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta)
 \geq\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_0}\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta)
 =\sup_P\mathbb E_P\mathcal L(U,\delta^0)
 \geq R_{\mathrm{hit}}. \tag{6}
\]
Taking the infimum over \(\delta\) and combining (4)--(6) proves equality for every bounded target-only loss on an arbitrary standard-Borel action space.

For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\) supplies the known kernel
\[
 \Pr(L_c=\ell\mid Z_c=z)=p_\ell B_{k\ell}/q_k. \tag{7}
\]
It is parameter-free and well defined because \(q_k>0\).  Thus a label-observing rule can be reproduced after label deletion by simulating (7), while forgetting the label gives the reverse comparison.  This proves label deletion.  A ranking vector is finite and therefore standard Borel, so the Han--Owusu--Shin ranking action is included.
statements.justification: This all-rule equality isolates exactly which Bernoulli observations can carry worst-case information about the target.
statements.gap: No named comparator proves a finite-sample all-measurable-rule deletion equivalence over unrestricted assignment-specific schedule marginals.
statements.consumer: It licenses full-experiment lower bounds and covers both deployment and ranking actions.

statements.statement:
For every fixed \(C\), fixed label-count vector, and bounded target-only loss \(\mathcal L\), regime \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) satisfies
\[
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{full}}(\alpha)))]
=
\inf_{\delta\in\mathfrak D_C}\sup_P\mathbb E_P[\mathcal L(U,\delta(\mathcal E_{C,CR}^{\mathrm{hit}}(\alpha)))].
\]
More generally, the equality holds after replacing the displayed finite deployment action space and its rule class by any standard-Borel decision space and all measurable randomized rules, provided the loss is bounded and target-only; this includes the ranking action of Han--Owusu--Shin.  Here the reduced experiment deletes the randomized label vector after the realized exact-count assignments are recorded.
statements.justification: The exact-count benchmark must be stated as its own randomization experiment.
statements.gap: Two-stage design papers retain strategy labels, while the exact count itself identifies the target slice in this menu.
statements.consumer: This gives the exact-count experiment equivalence for deployment and ranking decisions.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf B(p)\), \(\phi_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) is the canonical gradient of \(U_k\), with variance \(\tau_k^2/q_k\) and zero covariance across distinct slices. The full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_B^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_B^{(K)}.\] Its active restriction has covariance \(\Sigma_{B,A}=(\Sigma_B^{(K)})_{AA}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(g_z=\Pr(Z=z)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization}\), \(g_z=q_k/M_k>0\) for \(z\in\mathcal S_k\).  In the saturated conditional-outcome model, a regular submodel has a centered score \(s_z(Y(z))\) in cell \(z\); the known assignment law has zero score.  Differentiation of the target functional gives
\[
 \dot U_k(s)=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
 \mathbb E_{P_0}\!\left[(W(z)-\mu_z)s_z(Y(z))\right]. \tag{10}
\]
For \(\phi_k^B=q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z\in\mathcal S_k\}(W(Z)-\mu_Z)\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q^B_{P_0,p}}(\phi_k^Bs_Z)
 =\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\frac{q_k/M_k}{q_k}
 \mathbb E_{P_0}\!\left[(W(z)-\mu_z)s_z(Y(z))\right]
 =\dot U_k(s). \tag{11}
\]
The coordinate is conditionally centered and bounded by \(q_k^{-1}\), hence lies in \(L_0^2\), and it belongs to the direct sum of the conditional tangent spaces.  Equations (10)--(11) make it the unique tangent-space Riesz representer, hence the canonical gradient.  Its covariance is
\[
 \mathbb E(\phi_k^B)^2
 =\frac1{q_k^2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\frac{q_k}{M_k}
 \operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}=\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}, \tag{12}
\]
and \(\phi_j^B\phi_k^B=0\) pointwise for \(j\ne k\), because the slices are disjoint.

For a target cell \(z\), the law of large numbers gives \(N_z/C\to_Pg_z\).  On \(N_z>0\), the exact ratio identity followed by Slutsky's theorem yields
\[
 \sqrt C(\overline W_z-\mu_z)
 =\frac1{g_z\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf1\{Z_c=z\}
   \{W_c(z)-\mu_z\}+o_P(1). \tag{13}
\]
The fallback is negligible because \(\Pr(N_z=0)=(1-g_z)^C\leq e^{-Cg_z}\).  Averaging (13) over each finite slice and using \(M_kg_z=q_k\) gives jointly
\[
 \sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}
 =C^{-1/2}\sum_{c=1}^C(\phi_1^B(O_c),\ldots,\phi_K^B(O_c))'+o_P(1). \tag{14}
\]
The summands are iid, centered, and bounded.  For fixed \(a\in\mathbb R^K\), Taylor expansion of their characteristic function gives
\[
 \left(1-\frac{a'\Sigma_B^{(K)}a}{2C}+O(C^{-3/2})\right)^C
 \longrightarrow e^{-a'\Sigma_B^{(K)}a/2}. \tag{15}
\]
The Cram\'er--Wold device proves the asserted joint normal limit.

On the regular branch define
\[
 \widehat q_k=C^{-1}\sum_c\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\},\qquad
 \widehat\phi_{c,k}=\widehat q_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}
 \{W_c(Z_c)-\overline W_{Z_c}\}.
\]
The prescribed fallback handles undefined cells.  There are finitely many cells, each count diverges in probability, and all observations lie in \([0,1]\).  Cellwise laws of large numbers and the within-cell least-squares identity imply
\[
 C^{-1}\sum_{c=1}^C\widehat\phi_c\widehat\phi_c'\to_P
 \mathbb E\{\phi^B(\phi^B)'\}=\Sigma_B^{(K)}. \tag{16}
\]
Off-diagonal empirical products vanish identically.  Restricting (14)--(16) to \(A\) proves the final assertion.
statements.justification: This derives the full-vector calibrated score and primitive Bernoulli CLT that underlie the headline mechanism comparison.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is a nominal-label Horvitz--Thompson construction rather than the pooled assignment-calibrated canonical gradient.
statements.consumer: Every realized exact hit can contribute to full-menu welfare estimation and active-face policy selection.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\) with \(\alpha_k>0\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\), the full calibrated vector satisfies \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_C-U(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_C^{(K)}\to_P\Sigma_{CR}^{(K)}.\] Conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, its triangular-array influence coordinates are \(\phi_{c,k}^{CR}\).
statements.justification: This supplies the full-menu exact-count benchmark only when every reported policy receives a positive limiting share.
statements.gap: Existing two-stage variance formulas target direct and spillover contrasts rather than the full calibrated exact-slice welfare vector.
statements.consumer: It supports full-menu covariance estimation and rank inference under the benchmark mechanism.

statements.statement: Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), if \(\alpha_k>0\) only for every \(k\in A\), then \[\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N(0,\Sigma_{CR,A}),\qquad \widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\to_P\Sigma_{CR,A}.\] No estimator or covariance limit is asserted for an unallocated inactive policy.
statements.proof_tex:
Condition on the fixed-count label vector and restrict attention to \(k\in A\).  For each such \(k\), \(C_{C,k}/C\to\alpha_k>0\), so every active cell count diverges and direct ratio expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt C(\widetilde U_{C,k}-U_k)
 =\frac1{\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C\frac{C}{C_{C,k}}\mathbf1\{L_c=k\}
 \{W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c}\}+o_P(1). \tag{20}
\]
The active summands are centered and bounded, their cross-products vanish across distinct strata, and their conditional covariance converges to
\[
 \operatorname{diag}(\tau_k^2/\alpha_k:k\in A)=\Sigma_{CR,A}. \tag{21}
\]
The maximum normalized increment is \(O(C^{-1/2})\), so the conditional characteristic-function expansion proves the active Gaussian limit.  Replacing \(\mu_z\) by active cell means and applying the bounded conditional law of large numbers proves \(\widehat\Sigma_{C,A}\to_P\Sigma_{CR,A}\).  The nondegeneracy assumption makes (21) positive definite.  No expression in (20)--(21) involves an inactive stratum, so no result is claimed there.
statements.justification: The mechanism game needs only the positively allocated active tie face.
statements.gap: The full-menu CR limit is undefined at inactive zero-share coordinates; this proposition isolates the valid face experiment.
statements.consumer: It supplies the active covariance used by LAN, mechanism comparison, and oracle transfer.

statements.statement: Fix \(k\) with \(p_k>0\), and write \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}\). Han--Owusu--Shin Appendix-B Eq. (S1) is exactly \[\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}=\frac{1}{Cp_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k\}\frac{\gamma_k(Z_c)}{\beta_k(Z_c)}W_c(Z_c)=\frac{1}{C\eta_k}\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbf 1\{L_c=k,Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}W_c(Z_c).\] It has influence function \(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf 1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\) and \[\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k})=\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2\left(\frac1{\eta_k}-1\right).\] The best regular estimator in the nominal-label-\(k\) subexperiment has canonical gradient \(\phi_k^{nom}\) and efficiency bound \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\). Therefore, whenever \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), \[\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k}<\frac{\tau_k^2}{p_kB_{kk}}\leq\operatorname{AVAR}(\widehat U^{HOS}_{C,k}).\] If \(b_k^2>0\), assignment-cell calibration within the nominal subexperiment is itself strictly more efficient than Eq. (S1), apart from the additional Horvitz--Thompson participation term displayed above.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\),
\[
 \frac{\gamma_k(z)}{\beta_k(z)}
 =\frac{M_k^{-1}}{\pi_k^{m_k}(1-\pi_k)^{n-m_k}}=\frac1{B_{kk}}. \tag{22}
\]
Substitution in the Horvitz--Thompson formula, with \(\eta_k=p_kB_{kk}>0\), proves the displayed estimator identity.  Its iid summand has mean \(U_k\), because conditional assignment is uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\), and hence its exact influence coordinate is
\(\phi_k^{HOS}=\eta_k^{-1}\mathbf1\{L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}W(Z)-U_k\).  Furthermore
\[
 \mathbb E\{W(Z)^2\mid L=k,Z\in\mathcal S_k\}
 =\tau_k^2+M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mu_z^2
 =\tau_k^2+b_k^2+U_k^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\phi_k^{HOS})
 =\frac{\tau_k^2+b_k^2}{\eta_k}+U_k^2(\eta_k^{-1}-1). \tag{23}
\]
In the nominal-label target-hit subexperiment, each \(z\in\mathcal S_k\) occurs with probability \(\eta_k/M_k\).  The tangent-space calculation (10)--(12), with \(q_k\) replaced by \(\eta_k\), proves that \(\phi_k^{nom}\) is canonical and has variance \(\tau_k^2/\eta_k\).  Since \(b_k^2,U_k^2\geq0\) and \(0<\eta_k\leq1\), (23) is at least this bound.  If \(q_k>\eta_k\) and \(\tau_k^2>0\), positivity permits division and gives
\[
 \tau_k^2/q_k<\tau_k^2/\eta_k\leq\operatorname{Var}(\phi_k^{HOS}).
\]
Finally \(b_k^2>0\) makes the cell-heterogeneity term \(b_k^2/\eta_k\) strictly positive, independently of the nonnegative participation term.
statements.justification: This makes the closest same-target comparison exact at the estimator, influence-function, and variance levels.
statements.gap: HanOwusuShin2026 Appendix B proves unbiasedness of Eq. (S1) but does not derive the pooled efficient bound or separate its cell-heterogeneity and Horvitz--Thompson participation losses.
statements.consumer: Analysts can quantify both the cross-label gain and the additional gain from assignment-cell calibration over the published estimator.

statements.statement: In regime \(\mathsf B(p)\), the raw pooled estimator has influence function \(\psi_k\) and asymptotic variance \(\rho_k^2/q_k=(\tau_k^2+b_k^2)/q_k\). It is efficient if and only if \(b_k^2=0\). At \(n=4\), count-one assignment means \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\) give \(U_1=1/2\), \(\tau_1^2=4/25\), \(\rho_1^2=1/4\), and excess \(9/100\) before division by \(q_1\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(H_{c,k}=\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\) and \(N_k=\sum_cH_{c,k}\).  Since \(N_k/C\to_Pq_k>0\), the fallback is negligible, and ratio expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt C(\widehat U^{\mathrm{raw}}_{C,k}-U_k)
 =\frac1{q_k\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^CH_{c,k}\{W_c(Z_c)-U_k\}+o_P(1)
 =C^{-1/2}\sum_{c=1}^C\psi_k(O_c)+o_P(1). \tag{24}
\]
Uniformity of \(Z\) on \(\mathcal S_k\) and total variance give
\[
 \operatorname{Var}\{W(Z)\mid Z\in\mathcal S_k\}
 =\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\operatorname{Var}_P\{W(z)\}
 +\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}(\mu_z-U_k)^2
 =\tau_k^2+b_k^2. \tag{25}
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{Var}(\psi_k)=(\tau_k^2+b_k^2)/q_k\).  Comparing with the efficient bound \(\tau_k^2/q_k\) shows equality exactly when the sum of squares \(b_k^2\) vanishes.

For the witness, the four means average to \(U_1=1/2\).  A Bernoulli welfare bit of mean \(4/5\) or \(1/5\) has variance \(4/25\), so \(\tau_1^2=4/25\), while
\[
 b_1^2=\frac14\{4(3/10)^2\}=\frac9{100},\qquad
 \rho_1^2=\frac4{25}+\frac9{100}=\frac14. \tag{26}
\]
Copying the bit to all unit outcomes under its assignment produces a legal binary schedule, hence also a legal bounded schedule.  The excess before division by \(q_1\) is \(9/100\).
statements.justification: The variance decomposition identifies the exact calibration correction.
statements.gap: The supporting decomposition distinguishes within-slice assignment heterogeneity from the separate Horvitz--Thompson participation loss in HanOwusuShin2026 Eq. (S1).
statements.consumer: It tells analysts when raw pooling is safe and when cell calibration is necessary.

statements.statement:
Let \(A=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_kU_k(P_0)\), with \(|A|\geq2\), and suppose every policy in \(A^c\) is separated below the tied active welfare.  For every representative \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), including its common-shift component, the path \(\bar P_{C,h}=\bar P_{C^{-1/2},h}\) satisfies \(Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}\), \(dU_k(\bar P_{t,h})/dt|_{t=0}=h_k\), and
\[
\log\frac{d(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}{d(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}
=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^B-\frac12h^{\prime}I_Bh+o_{(Q^B_{P_0,p})^{\otimes C}}(1),
\qquad \Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B),
\]
with \(\dot\ell_k^B\in L^2_0(Q^B_{P_0,p})\) and \(I_B=\operatorname{diag}(q_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A)\).  Under \(\bar P_{C,h}\),
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow
N\{h,\Sigma_{B,A}\}.
\]
For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\) and every \(M<\infty\),
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A:\ \lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{(Q^B_{\bar P_{C,h},p})^{\otimes C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A).
\]
Moreover \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).  The same lower bounds hold for rules observing the full Bernoulli experiment by nuisance deletion.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(\sigma_z^2=\operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}\).  For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), Lemma \texttt{lem:exact-hit-factorization} gives
\[
r_z:=\Pr_0(Z=z)=\frac{q_k}{M_k}.
\tag{1}
\]
Every entry of \(B\) is positive because \(0<\pi_\ell<1\) and \(1\leq m_k\leq n-1\).  Since \(p\in\Delta_K\), (1) implies \(q_k>0\).  Assumption \texttt{ass:nondegenerate-active-slices} gives \(\tau_k^2\geq\underline\tau^2>0\) for \(k\in A\), so every division below is valid and \(I_B\) is positive definite.

First consider observational equivalence and the path derivative.  A cluster reveals the outcome vector at only its realized assignment.  The law \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_zP_{0,z}\) has the same marginal \(P_{0,z}\) as \(P_0\) at every assignment \(z\).  The randomization is independent of the schedule by \texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-schedule-independence}, so integrating the kernel \(R_{B,p}\) against either schedule law gives
\[
Q^B_{\bar P_0,p}=Q^B_{P_0,p}.
\tag{2}
\]
For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), write \(X_z=W(z)-\mu_z\).  Under \(P_{0,z}\), \(|X_z|\leq1\), \(\mathbb E_0X_z=0\), and \(\mathbb E_0X_z^2=\sigma_z^2\).  Hence the log moment-generating function in \texttt{def:least-favourable-path} satisfies
\[
\Lambda_{z,k}(0)=\Lambda'_{z,k}(0)=0,
\qquad
\Lambda''_{z,k}(0)=\sigma_z^2.
\tag{3}
\]
Differentiation is justified by the bounded support.  Indeed, on every fixed compact interval of tilt arguments the first three derivatives of \(\Lambda_{z,k}\) exist and are bounded uniformly over the finitely many target cells.  Therefore
\[
\Lambda_{z,k}(a)=\frac12a^2\sigma_z^2+O(|a|^3),
\qquad
\Lambda'_{z,k}(a)=a\sigma_z^2+O(a^2),
\tag{4}
\]
uniformly over those cells.  Since the tilted mean of \(W(z)\) equals \(\mu_z+\Lambda'_{z,k}(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\), (3) gives
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\mathbb E_{P_{t,h,z}}W(z)\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{h_k\sigma_z^2}{\tau_k^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
Using the definition \(\tau_k^2=M_k^{-1}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2\) and averaging (5) over \(\mathcal S_k\),
\[
\left.\frac{d}{dt}U_k(\bar P_{t,h})\right|_{t=0}
=\frac{h_k}{M_k\tau_k^2}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2
=h_k.
\tag{6}
\]
Moreover, (4) shows that, uniformly over every finite set of representatives \(h\),
\[
U_k(\bar P_{C,h})=U_k(P_0)+C^{-1/2}h_k+O(C^{-1}),
\qquad k\in A.
\tag{7}
\]
All assignment marginals outside the active target slices are fixed by the path.

We next derive local asymptotic normality from the primitive randomization.  For one observation, the likelihood ratio is one off the active target slices and, when \(Z=z\in\mathcal S_k\), is
\[
\exp\!\left\{\frac{h_kX_z}{\sqrt C\,\tau_k^2}
-\Lambda_{z,k}\!\left(\frac{h_k}{\sqrt C\,\tau_k^2}\right)\right\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus, with \(a_{C,k}=h_k/(\sqrt C\,\tau_k^2)\), the sample log likelihood ratio equals
\[
\sum_{c=1}^C\sum_{k\in A}\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}
\{a_{C,k}(W_c(Z_c)-\mu_{Z_c})-\Lambda_{Z_c,k}(a_{C,k})\}.
\tag{9}
\]
The linear part of (9) is \(h^{\prime}\Delta_C^B\).  By (1), the weak law of large numbers, and the definition of \(\tau_k^2\),
\[
\frac1C\sum_{c=1}^C
\mathbf1\{Z_c\in\mathcal S_k\}\sigma_{Z_c}^2
\longrightarrow_P
\frac{q_k}{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2
=q_k\tau_k^2.
\tag{10}
\]
Substituting (4) into the normalizer part of (9), using (10), gives its quadratic term
\[
-\frac12\sum_{k\in A}\frac{h_k^2q_k}{\tau_k^2}+o_P(1)
=-\frac12h^{\prime}I_Bh+o_P(1).
\tag{11}
\]
The sum of the cubic remainders is \(O(C^{-1/2}\max_{k\in A}|h_k|^3)\) for fixed \(h\).  The score coordinates are centered by (3), and disjointness of the slices together with (1) gives
\[
\mathbb E_0(\dot\ell_j^B\dot\ell_k^B)
=\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{q_k}{M_k\tau_k^4}
\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2
=\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{q_k}{\tau_k^2}.
\tag{12}
\]
They are bounded because \(|X_z|\leq1\) and \(\tau_k^2\geq\underline\tau^2\).  Assumptions \texttt{ass:iid-schedules}, \texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-iid}, \texttt{ass:bernoulli-label-schedule-independence}, and \texttt{ass:bernoulli-units} therefore make the score vectors iid, centered, and bounded.  The scalar Lindeberg condition holds for every linear combination, so the Cram\'{e}r--Wold argument yields
\[
\Delta_C^B\Rightarrow N(0,I_B).
\tag{13}
\]
Equations (9)--(13) prove the displayed LAN expansion, including the score in every common-shift direction \(h+c\mathbf1_A\).

For later use, we verify rather than assume uniform integrability of every likelihood ratio on a finite local parameter set.  Let \(L_C(h)\) denote the likelihood ratio in (9).  Independence across clusters and conditioning on the realized assignment give the exact identity
\[
\mathbb E_0L_C(h)^2
=\left[
1+\sum_{k\in A}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}r_z
\left\{\exp\bigl(\Lambda_{z,k}(2a_{C,k})
-2\Lambda_{z,k}(a_{C,k})\bigr)-1\right\}
\right]^C.
\tag{14}
\]
Boundedness of the third derivatives used in (4) implies
\(\left|\Lambda_{z,k}(2a)-2\Lambda_{z,k}(a)\right|\leq C_0a^2\) for all sufficiently small \(|a|\), uniformly over the finitely many cells.  Hence, for every finite \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^A\),
\[
\sup_{C\geq C_0'}\sup_{h\in\Theta}\mathbb E_0L_C(h)^2<\infty.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus \(\{L_C(h):C\geq1\}\) is uniformly integrable for each \(h\in\Theta\), and jointly so for the finite likelihood-ratio vector.  This is the required likelihood-ratio premise for the finite-prior passage below.

We also record the estimator limit jointly with the central sequence.  On the event that every active assignment cell is observed, whose complement has probability at most \(\sum_{k\in A}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}(1-r_z)^C\), ratio expansion of each cell mean gives
\[
\sqrt C\{\overline W_z-\mu_z\}
=\frac{1}{r_z\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C
\mathbf1\{Z_c=z\}\{W_c(z)-\mu_z\}+o_P(1).
\tag{16}
\]
The displayed complement probability tends to zero exponentially, so the prespecified empty-cell fallback contributes \(o_P(1)\).  Averaging (16) and using \(r_z=q_k/M_k\) yields
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,k}-U_k(P_0)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C\phi_k^B(O_c)+o_P(1).
\tag{17}
\]
Besides the variance calculation in \texttt{thm:efficient-exact-hit-bernoulli}, direct use of (1) gives
\[
\mathbb E_0(\phi_j^B\phi_k^B)
=\mathbf1\{j=k\}\frac{\tau_k^2}{q_k},
\qquad
\mathbb E_0(\phi_j^B\dot\ell_k^B)=\mathbf1\{j=k\}.
\tag{18}
\]
The bounded-vector central limit argument applied jointly to (17) and \(\Delta_C^B\) therefore gives a centered joint Gaussian limit with covariance blocks \(\Sigma_{B,A}\), \(I_B\), and the identity cross-block.  From (11), (13), (15), and (18), for every bounded continuous \(f\), change of measure gives
\[
\mathbb E_{\bar P_{C,h}}f\!\left(\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\right)
=\mathbb E_0\!\left[L_C(h)f\!\left(\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\right)\right]
\longrightarrow
\mathbb E f(Z+h),
\tag{19}
\]
where \(Z\sim N(0,\Sigma_{B,A})\).  To see the last equality explicitly, exponential weighting of the joint Gaussian limit by \(\exp\{h^{\prime}\Delta-h^{\prime}I_Bh/2\}\) changes the mean of the first block by \(\operatorname{Cov}(Z,\Delta)h=h\) and leaves its covariance equal to \(\Sigma_{B,A}\).  Uniform integrability in (15) justifies passing the expectation in (19).  This proves the asserted local Gaussian limit without assuming a limit law under the alternatives.

It remains to prove the all-rule local regret bound.  The inactive-action reduction must precede the finite-prior argument.  Let \(u_0=U_k(P_0)\) for \(k\in A\).  If \(A^c\neq\varnothing\), the stated separation and finiteness of \(\mathcal K\) give
\[
g:=u_0-\max_{j\in A^c}U_j(P_0)>0;
\tag{20}
\]
if \(A^c=\varnothing\), the following reduction is vacuous.  Fix \(a_0\in A\), and define \(\rho(a)=a\) for \(a\in A\) and \(\rho(a)=a_0\) otherwise.  For a finite set \(\Theta\subset\{h:\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\}\), (7) is uniform on \(\Theta\), while every inactive welfare is unchanged.  Consequently, for all sufficiently large \(C\), every active welfare exceeds every inactive welfare, simultaneously for \(h\in\Theta\).  Pointwise in the observed data and in any auxiliary randomization of a rule \(\delta_C\),
\[
\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})
\geq
\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\rho(\delta_C)}(\bar P_{C,h}).
\tag{21}
\]
For \(a\in A\), define the scaled active loss
\[
\ell_C(h,a)=\sqrt C\left\{\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_a(\bar P_{C,h})\right\}.
\tag{22}
\]
Equation (7) implies, uniformly on the finite set \(\Theta\times A\),
\[
\ell_C(h,a)\longrightarrow
\ell(h,a):=\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_a.
\tag{23}
\]
In particular the losses in (22) are uniformly bounded on \(\Theta\times A\).  This establishes the bounded-loss premise after, rather than before, inactive outputs have been removed.

For completeness, apply the finite-experiment lower-bound argument directly.  Let \(\nu\) be any prior on the finite set \(\Theta\), and represent the active-only randomized rule \(\rho\circ\delta_C\), conditional on the data, by its probability vector \(V_C=(V_{C,a})_{a\in A}\in\Delta_A\).  Along a subsequence attaining its limit inferior Bayes risk, tightness of \(\Delta_C^B\), compactness of \(\Delta_A\), and (11) permit extraction of a joint weak limit
\[
\left(\Delta_C^B,(L_C(h))_{h\in\Theta},V_C\right)
\Rightarrow
\left(\Delta,(L(h))_{h\in\Theta},V\right),
\quad
L(h)=\exp\{h^{\prime}\Delta-h^{\prime}I_Bh/2\},
\tag{24}
\]
where \(\Delta\sim N(0,I_B)\).  By (15), (23), and boundedness of \(V_C\), likelihood-ratio-weighted risks converge along this subsequence.  Set \(X=I_B^{-1}\Delta\), so \(X\sim N(0,\Sigma_{B,A})\) under the reference law, and define the randomized Gaussian rule
\[
\kappa_a(X)=\mathbb E(V_a\mid X),\qquad a\in A.
\tag{25}
\]
Because \(L(h)\) is measurable with respect to \(X\), conditioning in (25) preserves every limiting risk.  Hence
\[
\begin{split}
&\liminf_C\sum_{h\in\Theta}\nu(h)
\mathbb E_{\bar P_{C,h}}\!\left[\ell_C\{h,\rho(\delta_C)\}\right]\\
&\quad\geq
\inf_{\kappa}\sum_{h\in\Theta}\nu(h)
\mathbb E_{X\sim N(h,\Sigma_{B,A})}[\ell\{h,\kappa(X)\}],
\end{split}
\tag{26}
\]
where the infimum is over all measurable randomized Gaussian selectors.  Equation (26) is exactly the proved finite-prior lower-experiment conclusion: no convergence of the original, possibly inactive-valued rule was assumed.  Combining (21) with the fact that maximal risk dominates every prior average proves (26) as a lower bound for the original rule's local maximal regret.

We finally pass from finite priors to the full quotient ball while retaining the unknown common location.  Let \(d=|A|-1\), \(\mathcal H_M=\{u\in\mathbb R^d:\lVert u\rVert_2\leq M\}\), and choose the linear section
\[
S_A=D_A^{\prime}(D_AD_A^{\prime})^{-1},
\qquad D_AS_A=I_d.
\tag{27}
\]
Every representative is \(S_Au+c\mathbf1_A\).  On \(\mathcal H_M\), the loss is independent of \(c\) and is bounded by \(2\lVert S_A\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}M\).  By Lemma \texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}, invariant rules use
\[
D_AX\sim N(u,\Omega_A).
\tag{28}
\]
Because \(\Omega_A\) is positive definite, translation of its Gaussian density is continuous in \(L^1\).  Together with the displayed uniform loss bound and linearity of \(h\mapsto\ell(h,a)\), this gives a common modulus of continuity, over all randomized quotient selectors, for their risks as functions of \(u\in\mathcal H_M\).

Let \(\mathcal Q_\eta\) be a finite \(\eta\)-net of \(\mathcal H_M\).  The common modulus implies that the invariant minimax value on \(\mathcal Q_\eta\) converges to \(G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A)\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\).  On the finite grid, the closure of the attainable risk-vector set is a compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional cube: boundedness gives compactness after closure, and randomization gives convexity.  Separating this set from any strictly lower orthant shows that the finite-grid minimax value equals the supremum, over priors \(\nu\) on \(\mathcal Q_\eta\), of the invariant Bayes value.

It remains to realize that invariant Bayes value by finite priors in the full experiment.  Fix such a quotient prior \(\nu\).  For \(T>0\), average the common shift \(c\) uniformly on \([-T,T]\).  Given any full Gaussian rule \(\delta\), define
\[
\bar\delta_T(a\mid x)=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^T
\delta(a\mid x+c\mathbf1_A)\,dc.
\tag{29}
\]
Translation invariance of the loss and the Gaussian family gives the exact identity
\[
\sum_{u}\nu(u)R(S_Au,\bar\delta_T)
=\frac1{2T}\int_{-T}^T\sum_u\nu(u)
R(S_Au+c\mathbf1_A,\delta)\,dc.
\tag{30}
\]
For each fixed \(s\in\mathbb R\), the total variation between the action-probability vectors \(\bar\delta_T(\,\cdot\mid x+s\mathbf1_A)\) and \(\bar\delta_T(\,\cdot\mid x)\) is at most \(2|s|/T\), by cancellation of the overlapping portions of the two intervals in (29).  Taking weak-star limits of the bounded action-probability functions as \(T\to\infty\), first for rational \(s\) and then for all \(s\) by Gaussian \(L^1\)-translation continuity, produces an invariant rule.  Thus the infimum of the right side of (30) converges to the invariant Bayes value as \(T\to\infty\).  For fixed \(T\), the same Gaussian \(L^1\)-translation continuity is uniform over all rules and the finite quotient support, so a sufficiently fine finite grid of shifts has Bayes value arbitrarily close to the integral in (30).  We have therefore constructed a finite set of representatives, including a finite common-shift grid, whose finite-prior Gaussian Bayes value is arbitrarily close to the invariant Bayes value for \(\nu\).

Apply (26) to these finite priors, then let the common-shift mesh vanish, \(T\to\infty\), the quotient-net mesh \(\eta\downarrow0\), and the approximation errors vanish.  Equations (27)--(30) and the quotient reduction yield, for every measurable randomized rule sequence,
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{\bar P_{C,h}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})
-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,q_A).
\tag{31}
\]
The inactive policies have already been handled pointwise in (21), so no unbounded inactive-action loss enters the finite-prior argument.  Lemma \texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction} gives \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\) as \(M\to\infty\).

Finally, along this product-coupled path every nontarget marginal is fixed, and conditional on the retained target-hit record the deleted nontarget outcomes and nominal label information have a distribution independent of \(h\).  The reverse-kernel argument in \texttt{thm:nuisance-deletion-bernoulli} therefore applies to each finite local experiment, so a full-record rule cannot evade (31).

As an exact small-instance check, take \(n=4\), \((\pi_1,\pi_2)=(1/4,1/2)\), and the count-one slice.  Then \(M_1=4\), \(B_{11}=27/64\), \(B_{12}=1/4\), and \(q_1=(27/64)p_1+(1/4)p_2\).  Four independent tied welfare bits of mean \(1/2\) give \(\tau_1^2=1/4\), hence information \(q_1/\tau_1^2=4q_1\) and influence variance \(1/(4q_1)\).  For the assignment-heterogeneous model, let all four unit outcomes under a count-one assignment equal a Bernoulli bit whose four cell means are \((4/5,4/5,1/5,1/5)\).  This is a legal bounded within-cluster schedule, and all four cell variances are \(4/25\), hence information \(25q_1/4\) and influence variance \(4/(25q_1)\).  Thus both the tied target-bit submodel and the assignment-heterogeneous model have exactly the \(\tau_1^2/q_1\) covariance and \(q_1/\tau_1^2\) information derived above.  For two active policies, writing \(d=h_1-h_2\) and \(s^2=\tau_1^2/q_1+\tau_2^2/q_2\), the Gaussian rule choosing the larger coordinate has regret \(|d|\Phi(-|d|/s)\); this is also the symmetric two-point Gaussian testing lower bound.  Hence the two-point lower experiment matches the exact-hit pooled Gaussian regret rather than an iid nominal-label variance.

statements.statement:
Under \(\mathsf{CR}(\alpha)\), for every representative \(h\in\mathbb R^A\), including its common-shift component, the product-coupled path satisfies \(Q^{CR}_{\bar P_0,C_C}=Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}\) and
\[
\log\frac{dQ^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}{dQ^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}
=h^{\prime}\Delta_C^{CR}-\frac12h^{\prime}I_{CR}h+o_{Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}}(1),
\qquad \Delta_C^{CR}\Rightarrow N(0,I_{CR}),
\]
where, conditionally on the fixed-count label vector, \(\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR}\) is centered in its stratum and \(I_{CR}=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A)\).  Under \(\bar P_{C,h}\),
\[
\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}\Rightarrow N\{h,\Sigma_{CR,A}\}.
\]
For every measurable randomized rule sequence \(\delta_C\) and every \(M<\infty\),
\[
\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{h\in\mathbb R^A:\ \lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
\sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}
\left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]
\geq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A),
\]
and \(G_{A,M}\uparrow G_A\).  The independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) target-bit submodel has \(\tau_k^2=1/4\) and information \(4\alpha_k\); it is a witness, not a restriction on the general path.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(X_z=W(z)-\mu_z\) and \(\sigma_z^2=\operatorname{Var}_{P_0}\{W(z)\}\), and write \(\mathbb E_0\) for expectation under \(Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}\).  Boundedness of the potential outcomes gives \(|X_z|\leq1\).  For \(z\in\mathcal S_k\), differentiation of the finite moment-generating function gives
\[
 \Lambda_{z,k}(0)=\Lambda_{z,k}'(0)=0,
 \qquad \Lambda_{z,k}''(0)=\sigma_z^2.                    \tag{1}
\]
Because there are finitely many assignments and \(|X_z|\leq1\), the first three derivatives of every \(\Lambda_{z,k}\) are uniformly bounded on a fixed neighborhood of zero.  Taylor's formula applied to (1) therefore supplies a finite constant \(K_0\) such that, on that neighborhood,
\[
 \left|\Lambda_{z,k}(a)-\frac12a^2\sigma_z^2\right|
 \leq K_0|a|^3,
 \qquad
 \left|\Lambda_{z,k}'(a)-a\sigma_z^2\right|
 \leq K_0a^2,                                                   \tag{2}
\]
and, after enlarging \(K_0\),
\[
 \Lambda_{z,k}(2a)-2\Lambda_{z,k}(a)\leq K_0a^2.          \tag{3}
\]
These bounds are derived from bounded support, rather than imposed as regularity conditions.  Assumption \(\texttt{ass:nondegenerate-active-slices}\) gives \(\tau_k^2\geq\underline\tau^2>0\) on \(A\), so every division by \(\tau_k^2\) below is valid and the constants in (2)--(3) remain uniform over active coordinates.

We first identify the observed likelihood.  Conditional on a realized assignment array, cluster \(c\) reveals only the marginal outcome vector at \(Z_c\).  The marginal at that assignment is \(P_{0,Z_c}\) under both \(P_0\) and \(\bar P_0=\bigotimes_zP_{0,z}\).  Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:iid-schedules}\), \(\texttt{ass:cr-label-schedule-independence}\), and \(\texttt{ass:cr-exact-slices}\) then imply, after integrating over the same known randomization kernel,
\[
 Q^{CR}_{\bar P_0,C_C}=Q^{CR}_{P_0,C_C}.                  \tag{4}
\]
Fix \(h\in\mathbb R^A\) and set \(t_C=C^{-1/2}\) and
\(a_{C,k}=t_Ch_k/\tau_k^2\).  From \(\texttt{def:least-favourable-path}\), the conditional likelihood-ratio contribution of cluster \(c\), when \(L_c=k\in A\), is
\[
 \exp\!\left\{a_{C,k}X_{Z_c}
              -\Lambda_{Z_c,k}(a_{C,k})\right\};               \tag{5}
\]
clusters with labels outside \(A\) contribute one.  The comparison in (5) is against the right side of (4), so multiplying (5) over clusters is the likelihood ratio displayed in the theorem.

Condition on the complete label vector.  Assumptions \(\texttt{ass:iid-schedules}\) and \(\texttt{ass:cr-label-schedule-independence}\) make the cluster observations independent, and \(\texttt{ass:cr-exact-slices}\) makes \(Z_c\) uniform on \(\mathcal S_k\) in stratum \(k\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathbb E_0[\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR}\mid L]
 =\mathbf1\{L_c=k\}\frac1{M_k\tau_k^2}
   \sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\mathbb E_{P_{0,z}}X_z=0,            \tag{6}
\]
so the score is centered in its stratum.  Distinct score coordinates have zero product, while
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \frac1C\sum_{c=1}^C
 \mathbb E_0[(\dot\ell_{c,k}^{CR})^2\mid L]
 &=\frac{C_{C,k}}C\frac1{M_k\tau_k^4}
   \sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2\\
 &=\frac{C_{C,k}}C\frac1{\tau_k^2}
 \longrightarrow\frac{\alpha_k}{\tau_k^2},
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{7}
\]
where the second equality is the definition of \(\tau_k^2\), and the limit is \(\texttt{ass:cr-shares}\).  Thus the limiting covariance in (7) is
\[
 I_{CR}=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha_k/\tau_k^2:k\in A).           \tag{8}
\]
It is positive definite because every active \(\alpha_k\) is positive and every active \(\tau_k^2\) is at least \(\underline\tau^2\).

Here is a direct triangular-array central-limit calculation.  For fixed \(u\in\mathbb R^A\), put
\(\xi_{C,c}=C^{-1/2}u^{\prime}\dot\ell_{c,A}^{CR}\).  Boundedness and nondegeneracy give \(\max_c|\xi_{C,c}|\leq K_uC^{-1/2}\).  From (6), expansion of the conditional characteristic functions gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0(e^{i\xi_{C,c}}\mid L)
 =1-\frac12\mathbb E_0(\xi_{C,c}^2\mid L)+r_{C,c},
 \qquad
 \sum_{c=1}^C|r_{C,c}|\leq
 \frac16\sum_{c=1}^C\mathbb E_0|\xi_{C,c}|^3=O(C^{-1/2}).       \tag{9}
\]
Equations (7)--(9), followed by multiplication of the independent conditional characteristic functions, yield
\[
 \mathbb E_0\!\left[e^{iu^{\prime}\Delta_C^{CR}}\mid L\right]
 \longrightarrow \exp\{-u^{\prime}I_{CR}u/2\}.                 \tag{10}
\]
The conditional expression depends on the label vector only through its fixed counts, so (10) also holds unconditionally.  Since it holds for every \(u\), it proves
\(\Delta_C^{CR}\Rightarrow N(0,I_{CR})\).

We next expand the log likelihood.  By (2) and (5), its linear term is exactly \(h^{\prime}\Delta_C^{CR}\), and its quadratic term is
\[
 -\frac1{2C}\sum_{c:L_c=k\in A}
       \frac{h_k^2\sigma_{Z_c}^2}{\tau_k^4}.                    \tag{11}
\]
Conditional on the labels, the negative of twice (11) has expectation
\[
 \sum_{k\in A}\frac{C_{C,k}}C
       \frac{h_k^2}{M_k\tau_k^4}
       \sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\sigma_z^2
 =\sum_{k\in A}\frac{C_{C,k}}C\frac{h_k^2}{\tau_k^2}
 \longrightarrow h^{\prime}I_{CR}h.                            \tag{12}
\]
Its conditional variance is \(O(C^{-1})\), because the summands in (11) are independent and uniformly bounded and there are at most \(C\) of them.  Hence (12) and conditional Chebyshev give convergence in probability of (11) to \(-h^{\prime}I_{CR}h/2\).  The sum of the cubic remainders in (2) is bounded by
\[
 K_0\sum_{k\in A}C_{C,k}|a_{C,k}|^3
 \leq \frac{K_0}{\sqrt C}
       \sum_{k\in A}\frac{|h_k|^3}{\underline\tau^6}
 \longrightarrow0.                                              \tag{13}
\]
Combining (10)--(13) proves the asserted LAN expansion.  The same calculation holds jointly for every fixed finite collection of \(h\)'s, since all likelihood ratios are functions of the common central sequence and finitely many remainders tending to zero.

We record now the likelihood-ratio integrability that will be needed before invoking any local minimax result.  Let \(R_C(h)\) denote the likelihood ratio in (5), multiplied over clusters.  From (3), conditional independence, and uniform assignment within a stratum,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_0[R_C(h)^2\mid L]
 &=\prod_{k\in A}\prod_{c:L_c=k}
   \left\{\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
   \exp[\Lambda_{z,k}(2a_{C,k})-2\Lambda_{z,k}(a_{C,k})]\right\}\\
 &\leq
 \exp\!\left\{K_0\sum_{k\in A}C_{C,k}a_{C,k}^2\right\}\\
 &\leq
 \exp\!\left\{K_0\sum_{k\in A}h_k^2/\underline\tau^4\right\}<\infty .
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{14}
\]
The displayed calculation applies once every \(a_{C,k}\) lies in the neighborhood used in (2)--(3).  The omitted finite set of earlier second moments is finite because bounded support makes every exponential moment finite.  Thus \((R_C(h))_C\) is uniformly integrable for each fixed \(h\); for a finite parameter set the bound is uniform over all of its elements.  This verifies the required likelihood-ratio premise from primitive boundedness, rather than assuming contiguity or a limit theorem.

We next prove the local limit of the calibrated estimator.  The ratio expansion established in \(\texttt{prop:efficient-exact-hit-cr-face}\) is, coordinatewise on \(A\),
\[
 T_{C,k}:=\sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,k}-U_k(P_0)\}
 =\frac1{\sqrt C}\sum_{c=1}^C
   \frac{C}{C_{C,k}}\mathbf1\{L_c=k\}X_{Z_c}+o_{P_0}(1).        \tag{15}
\]
The principal term in (15) is
\((C\tau_k^2/C_{C,k})\Delta_{C,k}^{CR}\).  Therefore, jointly with the likelihood ratios for every fixed finite set of local parameters,
\[
 T_C=\Sigma_{CR,A}\Delta_C^{CR}+o_{P_0}(1),
 \qquad
 (T_C,\Delta_C^{CR})\Rightarrow
 (\Sigma_{CR,A}Z,Z),\quad Z\sim N(0,I_{CR}),                    \tag{16}
\]
because \(C\tau_k^2/C_{C,k}\to\tau_k^2/\alpha_k\), and \(\Sigma_{CR,A}=I_{CR}^{-1}\).  For \(s\in\mathbb R^A\), change of measure, (14), and (16) permit passage of the bounded factor \(e^{is^{\prime}T_C}\) through the likelihood ratio:
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \lim_C\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}e^{is^{\prime}T_C}
 &=\mathbb E\exp\!\left\{is^{\prime}\Sigma_{CR,A}Z
                   +h^{\prime}Z-\frac{1}{2}h^{\prime}I_{CR}h\right\}\\
 &=\exp\!\left\{is^{\prime}h-\frac{1}{2}s^{\prime}\Sigma_{CR,A}s\right\}.
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{17}
\]
The last equality is the moment-generating formula for the centered normal vector \(Z\).  Equation (17) is precisely
\[
 \sqrt C\{\widetilde U_{C,A}-U_A(P_0)\}
 \Rightarrow N\{h,\Sigma_{CR,A}\}                              \tag{18}
\]
under \(\bar P_{C,h}\).

For use in the regret argument, we also derive the local target expansion.  Under the tilted marginal at \(z\in\mathcal S_k\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_{t,h,z}}W(z)-\mu_z
 =\Lambda_{z,k}'(t h_k/\tau_k^2).
\]
The second inequality in (2) and the definition of \(\tau_k^2\) give, for \(k\in A\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 U_k(\bar P_{t,h})-U_k(P_0)
 &=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}
   \Lambda_{z,k}'(t h_k/\tau_k^2)\\
 &=t h_k+O(t^2h_k^2/\underline\tau^4).                          
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{19}
\]
Every inactive target slice is a nontilted marginal and therefore has exactly its baseline welfare.  In particular, (19) proves, uniformly over every fixed finite set \(\Theta\subset\mathbb R^A\) and \(a\in A\),
\[
 \ell_C(h,a):=\sqrt C\!\left\{
   \max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_a(\bar P_{C,h})\right\}
 \longrightarrow
 \ell(h,a):=\max_{k\in A}h_k-h_a.                              \tag{20}
\]
The convergence in (20) is uniform on \(\Theta\times A\), and the left side is uniformly bounded there after deletion of finitely many initial values of \(C\).

We now perform the inactive-action reduction before applying the finite-prior lower-bound lemma.  If \(A\ne\mathcal K\), finiteness of \(\mathcal K\) and the definition \(A=\operatorname*{arg\,max}_kU_k(P_0)\) give the strictly positive baseline gap
\[
 d_0=\min_{b\notin A}\left\{
        \max_{k\in A}U_k(P_0)-U_b(P_0)\right\}>0.               \tag{21}
\]
If \(A=\mathcal K\), set \(d_0=+\infty\).  Fix \(a_0\in A\).  Given a randomized rule \(\delta_C\), form \(\delta_C^A\) by leaving every output in \(A\) unchanged and replacing every output outside \(A\) by \(a_0\).  For a fixed finite \(\Theta\), (19) and (21) show that, for all sufficiently large \(C\), every active welfare exceeds every inactive welfare simultaneously for all \(h\in\Theta\).  Hence, pointwise in the observed data, in the auxiliary randomization of the rule, and in \(h\in\Theta\),
\[
 \max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})
 \geq
 \max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})-U_{\delta_C^A}(\bar P_{C,h}).   \tag{22}
\]
Thus no unbounded scaled loss from an inactive output is passed to the finite-prior lemma.  Equations (20) and (22) give an active finite action set, uniform boundedness of its local losses, and uniform actionwise convergence to \(\ell(h,a)\).

For completeness, we next show that finite priors suffice to recover the entire compact quotient Gaussian value, including the common-location nuisance.  Write \(d=|A|\), \(\Sigma=\Sigma_{CR,A}\), \(D=D_A\), and \(\Omega=D\Sigma D^{\prime}\).  Positivity in (8) and full row rank of \(D\) imply \(\Omega\) is positive definite.  Define
\[
 w=\frac{\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1_A}
         {\mathbf1_A^{\prime}\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1_A}.
\]
Then \(w^{\prime}\mathbf1_A=1\) and \(D\Sigma w=0\).  The map
\(x\mapsto(Dx,w^{\prime}x)\) is invertible because \(\ker D=\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf1_A\}\).  Let \(J\) be the linear map characterized by
\[
 DJ=I_{d-1},\qquad w^{\prime}J=0.                                \tag{23}
\]
Every \(h\in\mathbb R^A\) then has the unique representation
\(h=Jg+c\mathbf1_A\), where \(g=Dh\) and \(c=w^{\prime}h\).

In the Gaussian limit \(X\sim N(h,\Sigma)\), put \(Y=DX\) and \(S=w^{\prime}X\).  Equations (23) and \(D\Sigma w=0\) give
\[
 Y\sim N(g,\Omega),\qquad
 S\sim N\!\left(c,w^{\prime}\Sigma w\right),
 \qquad Y\ \text{and}\ S\ \text{are independent}.            \tag{24}
\]
The action loss is
\[
 \ell(g,a)=\max_{k\in A}(Jg)_k-(Jg)_a,                          \tag{25}
\]
which depends on \(g\), not on \(c\).  Equations (24)--(25) display explicitly why the common-shift coordinate is a statistical nuisance rather than a fixed known parameter.

Let \(\mathbb B_M=\{g\in\mathbb R^{d-1}:\lVert g\rVert_2\leq M\}\).  For a randomized quotient selector \(\kappa\), write \(R(g,\kappa)\) for its Gaussian risk.  These risks are equicontinuous in \(g\), uniformly over \(\kappa\).  Indeed, if \(f_g\) is the density of \(N(g,\Omega)\), the fundamental theorem of calculus gives
\[
 \int|f_g(y)-f_{g'}(y)|\,dy
 \leq \lVert g-g'\rVert_2
       \mathbb E\lVert\Omega^{-1}Z_\Omega\rVert_2,
 \qquad Z_\Omega\sim N(0,\Omega).                              \tag{26}
\]
The loss in (25) is Lipschitz in \(g\) and bounded on \(\mathbb B_M\).  Combining these facts with (26) produces a modulus \(\omega_M(r)\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 |R(g,\kappa)-R(g',\kappa)|
 \leq\omega_M(\lVert g-g'\rVert_2)                              \tag{27}
\]
for every selector \(\kappa\).

Choose a finite \(r\)-net \(\Gamma_r=\{g_1,\ldots,g_N\}\) of \(\mathbb B_M\), and let
\[
 V_r=\inf_\kappa\max_{1\leq i\leq N}R(g_i,\kappa).
\]
By (27) and the quotient characterization in \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\),
\[
 G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A)-\omega_M(r)
 \leq V_r\leq G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A).                       \tag{28}
\]
We give the finite minimax step rather than assuming a least-favorable prior.  Let \(\mathscr R\subset\mathbb R^N\) be the set of risk vectors
\((R(g_i,\kappa))_{i=1}^N\), and let
\(\mathscr C=\overline{\mathscr R+\mathbb R_+^N}\).  The set \(\mathscr C\) is closed and convex because selectors may be randomized.  If \(t<V_r\), then \(t\mathbf1_N\notin\mathscr C\); otherwise a sequence in \(\mathscr R\) would have coordinatewise maximum tending to at most \(t\), contradicting the definition of \(V_r\).  Choose a point \(x^\star\in\mathscr C\) minimizing Euclidean distance to \(t\mathbf1_N\).  Such a point exists: intersect \(\mathscr C\) with a closed ball centered at \(t\mathbf1_N\) and large enough to contain one fixed point of \(\mathscr C\), and minimize the continuous distance on that compact intersection.  Put \(\lambda=x^\star-t\mathbf1_N\ne0\).  For every \(x\in\mathscr C\), convexity puts \(x^\star+s(x-x^\star)\) in \(\mathscr C\) for \(0\leq s\leq1\).  The right derivative at zero of its squared distance from \(t\mathbf1_N\) is nonnegative, and hence \(\lambda^{\prime}(x-x^\star)\geq0\).  It follows that
\[
 \lambda^{\prime}(t\mathbf1_N)
 =\lambda^{\prime}x^\star-\lVert\lambda\rVert_2^2
 <\lambda^{\prime}x^\star
 \leq\inf_{x\in\mathscr C}\lambda^{\prime}x.                  \tag{29}
\]
Upward closure of \(\mathscr C\) forces every coordinate of \(\lambda\) to be nonnegative.  Normalizing gives \(\lambda\in\Delta_N\), and (29) becomes
\[
 \inf_\kappa\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_iR(g_i,\kappa)>t.              \tag{30}
\]
Thus, by taking \(t\uparrow V_r\), finite priors on finite quotient grids have Bayes values arbitrarily close to \(V_r\).

To retain rather than fix the common location, choose any nonempty finite symmetric grid \(\mathcal C_R\subset\mathbb R\) and form
\[
 \Theta_{r,R}=\{Jg_i+c\mathbf1_A:
                  i=1,\ldots,N,\ c\in\mathcal C_R\},           \tag{31}
\]
with product prior \(\lambda_i/|\mathcal C_R|\).  Every point in (31) satisfies \(\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M\).  Under this prior, (24) factorizes the likelihood: \(Y\) contains information only about \(g_i\), while \(S\) contains information only about the independently drawn common shift \(c\).  More explicitly, if \(f_i\) is the density of \(N(g_i,\Omega)\) and \(g_c\) is the density of \(N(c,w^{\prime}\Sigma w)\), then
\[
 \Pr\{i\mid Y=y,S=s\}
 =\frac{\lambda_i f_i(y)\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_R}|\mathcal C_R|^{-1}g_c(s)}
        {\sum_j\lambda_j f_j(y)\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_R}|\mathcal C_R|^{-1}g_c(s)}
 =\frac{\lambda_i f_i(y)}{\sum_j\lambda_j f_j(y)}.
\]
Since (25) is independent of \(c\), conditioning on \(S\) therefore cannot reduce the Bayes risk for choosing an action in \(A\).  Consequently the optimal Bayes risk in the full Gaussian experiment for (31) is exactly the left side of (30).  The grids \(\mathcal C_R\) may be arbitrarily large, so this construction does not treat the common shift as known.

We can now invoke \(\texttt{lem:lan-finite-prior-lower-bound}\), and all of its premises have already been verified.  Specifically, take the finite parameter set (31), the finite action set \(A\), the reference statistic \(I_{CR}^{-1}\Delta_C^{CR}\), and the likelihood-ratio vector \((R_C(h))_{h\in\Theta_{r,R}}\).  Equations (10)--(13) give their joint convergence to the likelihood ratios of \(N(h,\Sigma)\) relative to \(N(0,\Sigma)\); (14) gives coordinatewise uniform integrability; and (20) gives uniformly bounded, uniformly convergent active losses.  Equation (22) was established before this invocation and pointwise dominates the active-only rule's risk.  Therefore, for every original rule sequence \(\delta_C\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\liminf_{C\to\infty}\sup_{\lVert[h]\rVert_A\leq M}
 \sqrt C\,\mathbb E_{Q^{CR}_{\bar P_{C,h},C_C}}
 \left[\max_{k\in A}U_k(\bar P_{C,h})
       -U_{\delta_C}(\bar P_{C,h})\right]\\
 &\hspace{15mm}\geq
 \inf_\kappa\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_iR(g_i,\kappa)>t.
 \end{aligned}                                                   \tag{32}
\]
Choose \(r\) so that \(\omega_M(r)<\varepsilon/2\), and then choose
\(t>V_r-\varepsilon/2\).  Equations (28) and (32) give the theorem's lower bound minus \(\varepsilon\).  Since \(\varepsilon>0\) is arbitrary, the displayed local minimax bound follows.  The monotone limit
\[
 G_{A,M}(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A)\uparrow
 G_A(\tau_A^2,\alpha_A)
\]
is the final assertion of \(\texttt{lem:gaussian-quotient-reduction}\).  The likelihood calculation above was for the full record.  Because the exact treated counts are distinct, \(L_c\) is recoverable from \(Z_c\); \(\texttt{thm:nuisance-deletion-cr}\) supplies the corresponding all-rule target-only equivalence after deleting the randomized label vector, so no nontarget or label information has been silently credited to the lower experiment.

Finally, construct the target-bit witness by drawing independent bits \(B_z\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) for active target assignments, setting \(Y_j(z)=B_z\) for every unit \(j\), and setting all remaining schedule coordinates to arbitrary fixed values below \(1/2\).  Then on every active slice \(W(z)=B_z\), so \(\mu_z=1/2\), \(\sigma_z^2=1/4\), and
\[
 \tau_k^2=\frac1{M_k}\sum_{z\in\mathcal S_k}\frac14=\frac14.
\]
Substitution into (8) gives information \(\alpha_k/(1/4)=4\alpha_k\).  This is a legal bounded schedule law satisfying the fixed-cluster interference setup; independence of the bits is only an explicit witness and was not used to restrict the general path proved above.
